rows.table: Presidential primary results, March 1, 2016
rows.detail: The Republican town committee contest carries 45,963 blanks against 58,555 total votes -- the report prints the arithmetic of a 15-seat 'vote for many' contest without saying so. p191 also carries the SPECIAL STATE ELECTION for Precinct B only: Stephan Hay 399, Dean Tran 440.

rows.table: Assessments and revenues by major property class
rows.detail: TWO DEFECTS. (1) The Residential row prints its Valuation by Class as '21,174,263.21' -- a levy-sized number with cents, where the other rows carry whole-dollar valuations in the tens of millions; the class valuations as printed do not sum to the printed total 1,199,604,323. (2) The Open Space row present in FY2015 is absent entirely, so only four classes are listed against FY2015's five.

The addendum's Special Revenue Funds reprint is cleaner in structure than the main report's (which duplicates a page) but dirtier in digits (533,108.96 for 33,108.96, 'CHEck or Ticket' for 'GHSB Click It Or Ticket'), so neither copy is authoritative on its own -- the two have to be read against each other.

The report is materially incomplete, and an addendum exists to fix it. FIVE major tables are truncated or missing rows here -- the FY2016 receipts page loses its whole third column including the SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS and GRAND TOTAL; the Collection of Taxes table loses its ABATEMENTS, TRANSFER and BALANCES columns and its GRAND TOTAL, with the printed column header visibly shrinking from eight names on p47 to five on p48 to four on p49; the debt repayment schedule's last page carries a wrong FISCAL YEAR header; the employee compensation list starts part-way through the alphabet at BENOIT; and the Special Revenue Funds and employee compensation tables each contain a duplicated page.

The number of registered voters on the profile page (7115) is identical to FY2015's, in a year when 6,440 people voted in the November election and the Republican town committee ballot alone recorded 58,555 votes cast.

rows.table: Town and school employee compensation -- INCOMPLETE IN THIS DOCUMENT
rows.detail: This table has no heading and no printed total in either year, so a heading-driven search will not find it at all.

The single most valuable thing in it -- the GRAND TOTAL row of the FY2016 Collection of Taxes table -- appears nowhere else, and its FORWARD figure ($8,785,059.19) ties exactly to the closing figure of the same table in the FY2015 report, so the two years reconcile once this file is in hand.
The employee compensation pages recover surnames and department codes but not a single dollar amount, which makes the addendum's most personally identifying content also its least usable.

The Town Manager's report calls the FY2017 budget the FY2018 budget twice on page 18 -- 'passed a balanced budget for FY 2018 with an omnibus budget of $33,802,328' -- while the article that adopted that exact figure (p144) says FY2017.

The cemetery page prints a formal erratum against the previous year's report: 'Note: Correction to the 2015 Town Report: *James E. Steele, 84, North Cem. Korea/Vietnam Veteran / *Merelyn P. Foster Age 92 North Cem. Cremation'. It is the only place in either year where the town corrects its own published record.

The out-of-district special education placement count -- the number dollars cannot recover -- fell from thirty to nineteen in one year, and the report says so itself: 'nineteen (last year was thirty)', four collaborative, twelve day, three residential.

The fire department publishes a genuine workforce-tenure dataset: 52 call firefighters left over 2006-2016 against 24 retained, 47% of the department with 5 years' service or less, 29% with 20 or more.

The town election results are internally consistent this year and were not last year. Every FY2016 contest sums to 363 ballots; the FY2015 equivalent had a School Committee contest printing a total of 4,034 against candidate rows summing to 247.

rows.table: Town profile facts
rows.detail: REGISTERED VOTERS-7115 is UNCHANGED from the FY2015 report, which is implausible in a year with a presidential election that drew 6,440 ballots -- the line appears to have been copied forward.

Three sections of the same report disagree about the date of the town's own annual town meeting: the section heading and running head say May 5, 2016, while the Town Manager's report (p18), the Finance Committee's message (p64) and the August special town meeting's own Article 1 all say May 7, 2016.

A $4,000,000 debt exclusion for the Pavement Management Plan appears three times in three different forms and is never cross-referenced: as an authorised-unissued-debt line on p43, as a ballot question on p193 (passing 181 to 127 on 363 ballots), and as narrative on pp18 and 65.

It exists because the FY2016 report was published with five financial tables physically cut off at the right margin. The evidence is in the main report itself: the Collection of Taxes column header shrinks from eight column names on page 47 to five on page 48 to four on page 49, and then the table simply stops with no grand total.

The second most valuable thing -- the GRAND TOTAL of FY2016 receipts -- is in this document as a printed label but its VALUE was not recovered by OCR, so the town's total FY2016 revenue figure is not machine-readable in either PDF and has to be read off a page image.
